facts.text: - **Concept:** `$source` Operators - **Parent domain:** MongoDB Atlas Stream Processing - **Report type:** mechanism (internal parts, invariants, limits) - **Researched:** 2026-09-19

MongoDB's ASP Product Team maintains a public example repository, `mongodb/ASP_example`, described as both a human-readable corpus of examples and a RAG-optimised repository for code generation. Its canonical processor format is a JSON object with a `name` and a `pipeline` array whose first element is `{ "$source": { ... } }`. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/ASP_example

1. `$source` specifies the connection a stream processor streams data from, and is the ingestion point of the pipeline. — 2. `$source` must be the first stage of any pipeline it appears in. — 3. A pipeline may contain at most one `$source` stage. — 4. Once `$source` has ingested a document, ordinary MongoDB aggregation stages may transform it downstream. — 5. Documents in the source stream must be valid `json` or `ejson`; documents that are not are routed to the dead letter queue when one is configured. —; corroborated at — https://www.mongodb

`timeField` designates an authoritative timestamp for incoming messages and must be a `$toDate` or `$dateFromString` expression taking a source message field. If `timeField` is omitted, ASP creates a timestamp from the message timestamp provided by the source (for Kafka, the record's own timestamp, which is CreateTime by default and LogAppendTime only if the topic is configured that way; it is not generally broker receipt time). Event time is the time the source stream generates a document or the messaging system receives it, ascertained from the document's timestamp. `tsFieldName` overrides t

6. `timeField` sets the authoritative event timestamp and accepts only a `$toDate` or `$dateFromString` expression over a source field. When omitted, the source's own message timestamp is used. 7. Watermarks are applied only when the pipeline contains `$tumblingWindow`, `$hoppingWindow`, or `$sessionWindow`; a watermark updates only when a document arrives with a later event time than any previously consumed document. 8. With a Kafka `$source`, Atlas Stream Processing waits for all partitions to pass the watermark, so if a partition idles, the window doesn't close or output results. `partition

**F3 — Choosing a `$source` variant silently fixes your recovery story, not just your input.** A Kafka `$source` gives replayable offsets bounded by topic retention but **forfeits the built-in failover processor** (C69, C79). A change-stream `$source` gets failover but a hard recovery ceiling at the oplog window (C42, C73, C79). A Kinesis or cron `$source` also forfeits failover (C79). This coupling is stated nowhere in one place in the vendor docs; `practice.md` derived it and the other three reports supply its components.

This report covers only the `$source` aggregation stage of MongoDB Atlas Stream Processing and the set of source forms it accepts (Apache Kafka, MongoDB change streams at collection / database / cluster scope, AWS Kinesis, inline document arrays, cron schedules). It traces when each form appeared and identifies the primary and official sources for each.

9. The 31 July 2025 release added Initial Sync to `$source` when reading from Atlas collections, letting a processor ingest pre-existing documents as synthetic `insert` change events before tailing the change stream. ([MongoDB Docs, Changelog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/changelog/); field semantics in [MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

18. The Kafka form takes `connectionName` and `topic` as required fields, with optional `timeField`, `partitionIdleTimeout` (`size` + `unit`), `schemaRegistry.connectionName`, and a `config` sub-document carrying `auto_offset_reset` (default `"latest"`), `group_id` (auto-generated as `asp-${streamProcessorId}-consumer` when omitted), `enable_auto_commit`, `keyFormat` (default `"binData"`), and `keyFormatError` (`"dlq"` or `"passThrough"`). ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

23. The Kinesis form requires `connectionName`, `stream`, and `config.consumerARN`; `region` is required when the stream name exists in more than one region. Optional fields are `timeField`, `tsFieldName`, `shardIdleTimeout`, `config.initialPosition` (default `"LATEST"`), `config.atTimestamp`, and `config.reshardDetectionIntervalSecs` (default `300`). ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/); syntax block reproduced in [MongoDB Blog, 2026-01-07]

The document-array form takes a `documents` array (or an expression evaluating to one) and must not be combined with `connectionName`. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/

27. The cron form departs from standard cron semantics: when both day of month and day of week are restricted, a document is emitted only when **both** conditions match, whereas conventional cron implementations use OR. ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

Independent coverage confirms the product's existence and general availability but carries no stage-level detail: InfoWorld's GA article reports that MongoDB made Atlas Stream Processing generally available and describes it as an addition to the Atlas database-as-a-service, and it names no sources, field names, or limitations. Atlas Stream Processing is delivered as a capability of the Atlas service. Sources: https://www.infoworld.com/article/2337054/mongodb-atlas-stream-processing-is-finally-here.html

**F4 — `$source` is immutable in practice, and this is the most-corroborated non-obvious fact in the run.** All four reports independently reached C75 while citing **three different documentation pages** ([S2] architecture, [S3] limitations, [S9] manage-stream-processor). The practical consequence: iterate on source configuration with ephemeral `sp.process()` runs against a `documents` array before promoting (C7). The one apparent exception is X6, which is unresolved.

**D5 — The `$source` immutability rule and the failover procedure point in opposite directions.** Claim #23 says the `$source` stage cannot be modified while `resumeFromCheckpoint=true`. The failover procedure instructs operators to restart primary processors with `config.startAtOperationTime` set to the timestamp at which the failover processor stopped — which is a `$source.config` change. 52. Checkpoints record source offsets, not copies of source documents: oplog resume tokens for change-stream sources, partition offsets for Kafka sources. This makes `$source` the stage whose position defines restart behavior. 53. Restarting a processor queries the last committed checkpoint and resumes from the state it describes. 54. If the stored oplog resume token has fallen off the source cluster's oplog, ASP cannot resume from that checkpoint; recovery requires restarting with `resumeFromCheckpoint=false`, which discards the stored position. 55. initialSync.enable: true makes a change stream $source first ingest and process all existing documents in the collection as though they were insert change events, then proceed to new change events; initialSync.parallelism defaults to 1. initialSync cannot be combined with $hoppingWindow, $sessionWindow, or $tumblingWindow; the set of collections is fixed when the processor starts, collections created afterward are not synchronized, and if synchronizing any one collection fails the entire processor fails. initialSync might insert duplicate documents if it reads a change event during the collect

- A OneUptime article dated 2026-03-31 [S23] describes `$source` as supporting Apache Kafka and Atlas change streams only; another [S22] reduces it to "a Kafka topic or Atlas collection." - By that date Kinesis had been a documented source for ~4 months. Database- and cluster-wide change streams, the `documents` array, and cron are all absent from those accounts. - **Not a factual conflict — a staleness demonstration.** Two reports reached it independently ⟨H(D2), E(D3)⟩. Implication: for this concept, secondary sources go stale within months; the changelog [S5] is the only reliable indicator

- A third-party 2026 tutorial [S24] states ASP "requires a dedicated tier" (M10+). - MongoDB's own material [S2] describes stream processing **workspaces** with `SP2`–`SP50` tiers billed independently of the Atlas cluster tier. - The third-party claim appears to describe the change-stream **source cluster** requirement, not the stream processor. Unresolved; verify against current pricing before budgeting. ⟨P(gap 2)⟩

**What genuinely disconfirming evidence was found.** Real disconfirmation exists but it disconfirms *secondary accounts*, not the vendor's primary claims: X11 (Delbridge's stale same-project rule), X12 (OneUptime's incomplete variant list), X13 (the M10 tier claim). The vendor's own material supplies its own counterweights — the documented limitations, the Pub/Sub source/sink asymmetry (C86), the cron form's non-standard day semantics (C59) and absence of cost savings (C62), and the internal inconsistencies at X4, X6 and X10. That self-disconfirmation is worth something, but it is not external
